## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Hatthārohaputtattheragāthā* ("Verses of the Elephant Trainer's Son") is a short poetic text situated within the single-verse section of the *Theragāthā* (Thag 1.77) in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into multiple modern languages, with nine translations across eight languages indexed on SuttaCentral, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a full canonical parallel to this verse in the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 326) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also lists passage-level parallels across early Buddhist verse literature, notably with another discourse in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 19.1, the *Tālapuṭattheragāthā*), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 31 and UVS 31, *Cittavarga*), the Tibetan translation of the *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 31), and Chinese translations including the *Faju jing* (T 210.31), T 212.32, and the *Faji yaosong jing* (T 213.31) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse queries in DharmaNexus reported no additional Pali-internal or cross-linguistic alignments meeting the threshold [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
